skill.name: context-window-management
skill.description: Guides AI assistants on context window management, including summarization, trimming, routing, token prioritization, and avoiding context loss in long conversations.
skill.summary: Helps AI assistants preserve useful context while controlling token usage in long or complex conversations.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline code formatting in SKILL.md. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable behavior beyond prose guidance for context management.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 53 uses Markdown backticks to format related skill names, not Ruby or shell execution. The skill contains prompt guidance only and no executable code path.

content.value_statement: Long AI conversations often exceed token limits and lose important context. This skill provides strategies for summarization, trimming, routing, and prioritization.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to choose summarization, trimming, retrieval, or routing based on context size.
Guides placement of important details near the start and end of prompts.
Helps prioritize context by relevance, importance, and token cost.
Identifies common context management anti-patterns such as naive truncation.
Supports planning for long conversations and multi-turn AI workflows.
limitations: Does not count tokens with a specific tokenizer.
Does not implement memory storage, retrieval, or prompt caching code.
Does not connect to external data sources or model APIs.
Requires the user to provide the conversation or context constraints.

use_cases.title: Design Long-Running Assistants
use_cases.description: Plan how an assistant should preserve instructions, decisions, and user preferences across long conversations.

use_cases.title: Control Token Costs
use_cases.description: Choose what to keep, summarize, or remove when prompts are too large for reliable model use.

use_cases.title: Improve Prompt Reliability
use_cases.description: Structure context so critical requirements stay visible and less important material does not crowd the prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing prompt or conversation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt or conversation for context window risks. Identify what to keep, summarize, move, or remove.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Context Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a long-running assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a context management plan for this assistant. Include stable instructions, recent turns, summaries, retrieval needs, and token priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Lost-in-the-Middle Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced restructuring for important information placement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Restructure this context to reduce lost-in-the-middle risk. Put critical goals, constraints, and decisions where the model will use them reliably.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Routing Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for multiple context sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a context routing strategy for this workflow. Define when to use full context, summaries, retrieved facts, or task-specific context slices.

output_examples.input: A support assistant has long tickets, product docs, and user history in one prompt.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: keep current ticket details verbatim, summarize old user history, retrieve only relevant product sections, and place escalation rules last.

output_examples.input: A coding assistant loses project requirements after many turns.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: maintain a short decision summary, keep active constraints near the top, and remove resolved debugging details after each milestone.

output_examples.input: A research workflow combines many notes before asking for synthesis.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: group notes by source and relevance, summarize low-value material, and preserve direct evidence for claims that need citation.

best_practices: Rank context by task relevance before adding it to the prompt.
Preserve critical constraints verbatim and summarize supporting history.
Review context after major task changes so stale details do not guide the model.
anti_patterns: Pasting all available history without ranking importance.
Removing the oldest text without checking whether it contains key decisions.
Using one context strategy for every task size and risk level.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps manage limited context windows through summarization, trimming, routing, and prioritization.

faq.question: Can it count exact tokens?
faq.answer: No. It gives strategy guidance, but it does not include a tokenizer or counting tool.

faq.question: Does it store conversation memory?
faq.answer: No. It can guide memory design, but it does not implement storage or retrieval.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for short prompts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help decide which details are essential before context becomes too large.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The source is prompt guidance, and the detected command pattern was Markdown formatting.
